basis: Preeclampsia is defined by pregnancy-associated hypertension with proteinuria or organ dysfunction; renal glomerular endotheliosis is characteristic. Eclampsia is a minority manifestation.
Nonsyndromic congenital sensorineural hearing loss.
Polycystic renal disease with advanced renal failure; hypertension in 16/20 and ventricular hypertrophy in 2/2 support cardiovascular involvement. Hepatic cysts only 2/20.
Severe skeletal dysplasia affecting vertebrae and other bones; additional organ disease varies by subtype.
Carcinoma originates in the maxillary sinus, part of the upper respiratory tract.
Corneal stromal dystrophy defines the disease, even though its opacities generally do not impair vision.
Fibrous dysplasia directly replaces normal bone in a single skeletal site.
Inherited dystrophy of the vitreous and retina; the neurological ancestor does not establish extraocular disease.
Defining eyelid coloboma, abnormal hair pattern and anorectal malformations; developmental delay occurs in only 1/10.
X-linked neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability in 10/10; macrocephaly alone does not establish skeletal disease.
Inherited calcium/phosphate metabolic disorder; intrinsic renal phosphate wasting and nephrocalcinosis in 15/15 establish common renal involvement.
Inherited tyrosine/melanin metabolism disorder defined by skin and hair hypopigmentation and ocular abnormalities with reduced visual acuity.
Epilepsy beginning within the first year of life; additional organ involvement is not shared across this umbrella.
Neurodevelopmental impairment is shared across the major chromosome 15 syndromes listed; endocrine and structural organ abnormalities are subtype-dependent.
Progressive cerebellar degeneration and movement disorder; abnormal eye movements are neurologic. Hypogonadism and skeletal abnormalities are occasional.
Capillaria nematode infection; predominant human intestinal disease directly injures intestinal mucosa. Hepatic and pulmonary forms are uncommon variants.
Carcinoma originates in the epithelial lining of the esophagus.
Renal tubular transport disorder defined by hyperkalemia, hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis and hypertension.
Isolated defective spermatogenesis and sperm motility cause male infertility; no endocrine or other covered organ disorder is established.
Hereditary tumor association defined by cutaneous melanoma and neural system tumors, typically astrocytoma; no additional organs inferred from cancer risk.
Choanal atresia, hearing loss and cardiac septal defects define the syndrome; eyelid coloboma occurs in 12/14. Renal anomalies are uncommon.
Transient antenatal renal tubular salt-wasting disorder with characteristic sodium, potassium and chloride disturbances.
Brain, eye and renal abnormalities define syndrome; intestinal malrotation reported in 2/3. Endocrine and hearing findings each reported in one case, omitted under cap.
Immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease causing direct intestinal inflammation; associated extraintestinal diseases are not established for this subtype.
Intellectual disability, seizures and spastic diplegia define neurologic disease; lumbar hyperlordosis and genu valgum occur in the reported patient (1/1).
